faqs.q: When is the best time to see the Great Migration in Serengeti?
faqs.a: July–October for Mara River crossings in northern Serengeti; January–March for calving in the south / Ndutu; May–June for Grumeti crossings in the Western Corridor. Rainfall can shift timing by weeks.

faqs.q: Is Tanzania or Kenya better for the migration?
faqs.a: Tanzania hosts herds for most of the year and exclusive events like Ndutu calving and Grumeti crossings. Mara crossings can be viewed from northern Serengeti or Kenya’s Maasai Mara — Serengeti often feels less vehicle-dense and pairs naturally with Ngorongoro.

faqs.q: How much does a migration safari cost?
faqs.a: Private mid-range northern safaris often land in the mid-hundreds of USD per person per day all-in; northern camps in peak crossing season cost more. Get a dated quote from our Arusha team for exact inclusions.

faqs.q: How many days should I book?
faqs.a: Plan at least 3–5 nights in Serengeti for migration focus (often inside a 6–8 day circuit). Crossing seasons benefit from extra buffer nights in the right region.
